DAE Integration and Island Support Design

Status: Phases 1-4 Implemented, Terminal-ExtParam Refactor Complete Created: 2025-01-29 Updated: 2025-01-30 Author: Design discussion with user

Executive Summary

This document describes the architectural decisions for DAE integration, generic variable access, and island support in Powerful.jl.

Completed Work:

  • Phase 1: DAE as SystemModel field ✓
  • Phase 2: Generic variable accessors ✓
  • Phase 3: Topology analysis with Terminal API ✓
  • Phase 4: Island splitting ✓
  • Terminal-ExtParam unification (breaking change discovered during Phase 4) ✓

Future Work:

  • Phase 5: Multi-island unified accessors (not started)
  • Phase 6: Documentation and examples (not started)

Core Principle: Generic interfaces eliminate model-specific code through systematic composition of IndexOrder (external→internal), AddressManager (variable→address), and DAE (address→value).

Design Decisions

Decision 1: DAE as SystemModel Field

Problem: DAE created separately from SystemModel, requiring manual lifecycle management and synchronization.

Solution: Make DAE an optional field of SystemModel, created automatically during setup!().

Rationale:

  • Lifecycle coupling: DAE dimensions depend on AddressManager assignments → create after setup
  • Convenience: Most workflows need DAE → default to creating it automatically
  • Flexibility: Allow create_dae=false for specialized use cases
  • Backward compatibility: Existing code creating separate DAE continues to work

Implementation: Added dae::Union{Nothing, DAE} field to SystemModel, created in constructor after setup!() when auto_setup=true && create_dae=true.

Decision 2: Generic Variable Accessors

Problem: Accessing variables requires manual composition of IndexOrder, AddressManager, and DAE, or 100+ model-specific functions.

Solution: Provide unified interface get_var(sys, model, var, ext_key) that composes the three systems automatically.

Rationale:

  • Composability: IndexOrder (ext→int) + AddressManager (var→addr) + DAE (addr→value) = complete generic access
  • Type safety: Leverage existing validated systems rather than new abstractions
  • Zero model-specific code: Works for any variable in any model automatically
  • Discoverability: Single consistent pattern replaces scattered model-specific functions

API Design:

  • get_var(sys, model, var, ext_key) - Primary interface using external keys
  • get_var_by_index(sys, model, var, idx) - Performance path using internal indices
  • get_all_vars / get_vars_dict - Complementary operations
  • Equivalent functions for residuals

Implementation: variable_accessors.jl

Decision 3: Terminal API for Topology

Problem: Island detection requires knowing model connectivity, but hardcoding field names (:i, :fbus, :bus) violates extensibility principles.

Solution: Declarative Terminal API where models declare connectivity via get_terminals().

Rationale:

  • Extensibility: New models declare terminals → topology analysis works automatically
  • Hybrid systems: Supports multiple vertex types (AC buses, DC nodes, etc.)
  • Multi-terminal devices: Supports N-terminal devices (2-winding, 3-winding transformers, etc.)
  • Single source of truth: Terminal declarations used by both topology and data retrieval

Design:

struct Terminal
    vertex_model::Symbol  # Which model type (e.g., :Bus)
    field::Symbol         # Which field in model (e.g., :i, :fbus)
end

# Models declare connectivity
PowerCore.get_terminals(::Type{Branch}) = (
    Terminal(:Bus, :i),  # From bus
    Terminal(:Bus, :j)   # To bus
)

Implementation: topology.jl and model files

Decision 4: Terminal-ExtParam Unification (Breaking Change)

Problem: Terminal (topology) and ExtParam (data retrieval) both encoded connectivity information separately, violating DRY principle.

Solution: Make ExtParam use Terminal as base type, eliminating duplication.

Rationale:

  • DRY: Single declaration of connectivity used by both systems
  • Consistency: Same Terminal object describes topology and data flow
  • Type safety: Terminal is a struct, not loose Symbol fields
  • Maintainability: Changes to connectivity happen in one place

Breaking Change:

# OLD (before)
ExtParam(:basekv, :terminal, :Bus, :basekv, :i, BaseVoltage(), ...)
#                 ^^^^^^^^^  ^^^^           ^^
#                 Duplicate connectivity info

# NEW (after)
terminal = Terminal(:Bus, :i)
ExtParam(:basekv, terminal, :basekv, BaseVoltage(), ...)
#                 ^^^^^^^^
#                 Single source of truth

Migration: All models updated to declare TERMINALS constants, ExtParam definitions reference these constants.

Implementation: core_types.jl, all model files

Decision 5: Islands as Vector{SystemModel}

Problem: Multi-island systems could require specialized container types and access methods.

Solution: Islands are just Vector{SystemModel} - no special abstractions.

Rationale:

  • Composition: Each island is a complete, independent SystemModel
  • Reusability: All existing APIs (solvers, accessors) work on islands without modification
  • Parallel solving: pmap(solve_powerflow, islands) just works
  • Simplicity: No new types to learn or maintain

Island Extraction:

  • Each island gets own AddressManager (independent address space)
  • Each island gets own IndexOrder (renumbered 1:n, preserving external keys)
  • Each island gets own DAE (independent y, g arrays)
  • ExtParam indexers rebuilt via ext2int() during island setup

Implementation: split_islands(sys) in topology.jl

Key APIs

Variable Access

# Get single variable by external key
voltage = get_var(sys, :Bus, :v, 4001)

# Get all variables (in internal order)
all_voltages = get_all_vars(sys, :Bus, :v)

# Get as dictionary (keyed by external keys)
voltage_dict = get_vars_dict(sys, :Bus, :v)

Topology Analysis

# Analyze connectivity and identify islands
topo = analyze_topology(sys)
println("Found $(topo.n_islands) islands")

# Cache in SystemModel
analyze_topology!(sys)  # Sets sys.topology

Island Splitting

# Extract independent SystemModel per island
islands = split_islands(sys)

# Each island is a full SystemModel - solve independently
for island in islands
    sol = solve_powerflow(island)
end

# Or in parallel
solutions = pmap(solve_powerflow, islands)

Architecture Summary

Data Flow

  1. Parse: Raw data → SystemModel with external keys preserved
  2. Setup: setup!(sys) assigns addresses and creates IndexOrder
  3. DAE Creation: sys.dae created automatically with proper dimensions
  4. Variable Access: External key → internal index → address → value (via get_var)

Type Composition

SystemModel
├── AddressManager (variable/residual → address mapping)
├── IndexOrder (external key → internal index mapping)
├── DAE (address → value storage)
├── models (StructArrays of model data)
└── topology (cached connectivity analysis)

Island Independence

Each island in split_islands(sys) is a complete SystemModel with:

  • Independent address space (own AddressManager)
  • Local internal indices 1:n (own IndexOrder)
  • Preserved external keys (bus numbers unchanged)
  • Independent DAE arrays (own y, g vectors)

This enables parallel solving and modular analysis.

Benefits

Code Simplification

  • Before: 100+ model-specific getter/setter functions
  • After: ~10 generic functions handle all models

Consistency

  • Before: Different patterns per model type (get_bus_voltage, get_pq_power, etc.)
  • After: One unified pattern: get_var(sys, model, var, key)

Extensibility

  • Before: New model requires writing custom accessor functions
  • After: New model works automatically via AddressManager + Terminal API

Island Support

  • Before: Would require specialized container types and access methods
  • After: Islands are Vector{SystemModel} - same APIs work unchanged

Conclusion

This architecture provides a clean, composable system where:

Get variable value using external key (e.g., bus number).

Generic function that works for any variable in any model by combining:

  1. IndexOrder: external key → internal array index
  2. AddressManager: model/variable → DAE addresses
  3. DAE: addresses → actual values

Arguments

  • sys::SystemModel: System model (must have order and dae)
  • model::Symbol: Model name (:Bus, :PQ, :PV, etc.)
  • var::Symbol: Variable name (:v, :theta, :p, etc.)
  • ext_key: External key for lookup (bus number, or tuple for composite keys)

Returns

  • Variable value (type matches sys.dae.y element type)

Examples

# Bus voltage by external bus number
v = get_var(sys, :Bus, :v, 4001)

# Bus angle by external bus number
θ = get_var(sys, :Bus, :theta, 4001)

# PQ load power (composite key: bus number + load id)
p = get_var(sys, :PQ, :p, (4001, "1"))

# Branch flow (composite key: from bus, to bus, circuit id)
p_flow = get_var(sys, :Branch, :p_i, (4001, 4002, "1"))

Errors

  • If sys.order is nothing: Error (IndexOrder required)
  • If sys.dae is nothing: Error (DAE not created)
  • If external key not found: KeyError from IndexOrder
  • If model/variable not found: Error from AddressManager

""" function getvar(sys::SystemModel, model::Symbol, var::Symbol, extkey) # Validate preconditions isnothing(sys.order) && error( "SystemModel has no IndexOrder - cannot map external keys. " * "Use getvarbyindex() for direct internal index access." ) isnothing(sys.dae) && error( "SystemModel has no DAE - call setup! with createdae=true" )

# Step 1: External key → internal index
if !haskey(sys.order.indices, model)
    error("Model :$model not found in IndexOrder")
end
internal_idx = sys.order.indices[model][ext_key]

# Step 2: Get addresses for this variable
addrs = get_var_addresses(sys.address_manager, model, var)

# Step 3: Return value from DAE
return sys.dae.y[addrs[internal_idx]]

end

""" getvarby_index(sys::SystemModel, model::Symbol, var::Symbol, idx::Int) -> T

Get variable value using internal array index (zero-based indexing).

Faster than get_var() since it skips external→internal mapping. Use when you already have internal indices.

Arguments

  • sys::SystemModel: System model (must have dae)
  • model::Symbol: Model name
  • var::Symbol: Variable name
  • idx::Int: Internal array index (1-based)

Example

# Direct access by internal index (no external key lookup)
v = get_var_by_index(sys, :Bus, :v, 1)  # First bus in internal ordering

""" function getvarbyindex(sys::SystemModel, model::Symbol, var::Symbol, idx::Int) isnothing(sys.dae) && error("SystemModel has no DAE") addrs = getvaraddresses(sys.addressmanager, model, var) return sys.dae.y[addrs[idx]] end

""" getallvars(sys::SystemModel, model::Symbol, var::Symbol) -> Vector

Get all values for a variable across all instances (in internal order).

Example

# Get all bus voltages
voltages = get_all_vars(sys, :Bus, :v)

# Get all PQ load powers
pq_powers = get_all_vars(sys, :PQ, :p)

""" function getallvars(sys::SystemModel, model::Symbol, var::Symbol) isnothing(sys.dae) && error("SystemModel has no DAE") addrs = getvaraddresses(sys.address_manager, model, var) return sys.dae.y[addrs] end

""" getvarsdict(sys::SystemModel, model::Symbol, var::Symbol) -> Dict

Get all values as a dictionary keyed by external keys.

Useful for exporting results with semantic bus numbers.

Example

# Get bus voltages indexed by external bus number
voltages = get_vars_dict(sys, :Bus, :v)
# Dict(1 => 1.06, 2 => 1.045, 4001 => 1.02, ...)

""" function getvarsdict(sys::SystemModel, model::Symbol, var::Symbol) isnothing(sys.order) && error("SystemModel has no IndexOrder") isnothing(sys.dae) && error("SystemModel has no DAE")

result = Dict()
addrs = get_var_addresses(sys.address_manager, model, var)

for (ext_key, internal_idx) in sys.order.indices[model]
    result[ext_key] = sys.dae.y[addrs[internal_idx]]
end

return result

end

export getvar, getvarbyindex export getallvars, getvarsdict


#### Residual Accessors (Same Pattern)

julia """ getres(sys::SystemModel, model::Symbol, res::Symbol, extkey) -> T

Get residual value using external key.

Same pattern as get_var() but for residuals. """ function getres(sys::SystemModel, model::Symbol, res::Symbol, extkey) isnothing(sys.order) && error("SystemModel has no IndexOrder") isnothing(sys.dae) && error("SystemModel has no DAE")

internal_idx = sys.order.indices[model][ext_key]
addrs = get_res_addresses(sys.address_manager, model, res)
return sys.dae.g[addrs[internal_idx]]

end

Similar functions: getresbyindex, getallres, getres_dict


### Part 3: Topology Analysis and Island Detection

Create new file: `src/topology/topology.jl`

julia """ TopologyInfo

Network topology analysis results.

Fields

  • n_islands::Int: Number of disconnected islands
  • island_map::Vector{Int}: Maps bus internal index → island number (1-based)
  • slack_buses::Vector{Int}: Slack bus internal index per island
  • adjacency::SparseMatrixCSC{Bool}: Bus connectivity matrix
  • components::Vector{Vector{Int}}: Bus internal indices per island

""" struct TopologyInfo nislands::Int islandmap::Vector{Int} slack_buses::Vector{Int} adjacency::SparseMatrixCSC{Bool, Int} components::Vector{Vector{Int}} end

""" analyze_topology(sys::SystemModel) -> TopologyInfo

Analyze power system topology to identify islands and connectivity.

Must be called AFTER setup!(sys) so addresses are assigned.

Algorithm

  1. Build adjacency matrix from Branch/Transformer models
  2. Filter by status (only active branches)
  3. Run connected components algorithm (BFS/DFS)
  4. Identify slack bus per island (or warn if missing)

Example

sys = SystemModel(case)  # setup!() called automatically
topo = analyze_topology(sys)

println("Found \$(topo.n_islands) islands")
for i in 1:topo.n_islands
    buses = topo.components[i]
    println("Island \$i: \$(length(buses)) buses")
end

Caching

# Cache in SystemModel for reuse
sys.topology = analyze_topology(sys)

# Or use analyze_topology! to cache automatically
analyze_topology!(sys)  # Sets sys.topology

""" function analyzetopology(sys::SystemModel) # Validate setup if !issetup(sys) error("SystemModel must be set up before topology analysis. Call setup!(sys).") end

# Extract Bus data
if !haskey(sys.models, :Bus)
    error("Cannot analyze topology: no Bus model found")
end
n_buses = length(sys.models.Bus)

# Build adjacency matrix from branches
adj = spzeros(Bool, n_buses, n_buses)

# Add Branch connections
if haskey(sys.models, :Branch)
    _add_branch_connections!(adj, sys.models.Branch, sys.order)
end

# Add Transformer connections
if haskey(sys.models, :Transformer2W)
    _add_transformer_connections!(adj, sys.models.Transformer2W, sys.order)
end

# Make symmetric (undirected graph)
adj = adj .| adj'

# Find connected components
island_map, n_islands = _find_connected_components(adj, n_buses)
components = _group_by_island(island_map, n_islands)

# Identify slack buses per island
slack_buses = _find_slack_per_island(sys.models.Bus, island_map, n_islands)

return TopologyInfo(n_islands, island_map, slack_buses, adj, components)

end

""" analyze_topology!(sys::SystemModel) -> TopologyInfo

Analyze topology and cache result in sys.topology.

Returns the TopologyInfo and stores it in the SystemModel. """ function analyzetopology!(sys::SystemModel) sys.topology = analyzetopology(sys) return sys.topology end

Helper functions

function addbranchconnections!(adj, branches, order) # Map external bus numbers to internal indices busorder = order.indices[:Bus]

for i in 1:length(branches)
    # Skip inactive branches
    if branches.st[i] == 0
        continue
    end

    # Get internal bus indices
    fbus_internal = bus_order[branches.fbus[i]]
    tbus_internal = bus_order[branches.tbus[i]]

    # Add edge (undirected)
    adj[fbus_internal, tbus_internal] = true
    adj[tbus_internal, fbus_internal] = true
end

end

function findconnectedcomponents(adj::SparseMatrixCSC, n::Int) visited = falses(n) islandmap = zeros(Int, n) island_num = 0

# BFS for each unvisited component
for start in 1:n
    if visited[start]
        continue
    end

    island_num += 1
    queue = [start]
    visited[start] = true
    island_map[start] = island_num

    while !isempty(queue)
        node = popfirst!(queue)

        # Visit neighbors
        for neighbor in findnz(adj[:, node])[1]
            if !visited[neighbor]
                visited[neighbor] = true
                island_map[neighbor] = island_num
                push!(queue, neighbor)
            end
        end
    end
end

return island_map, island_num

end

function groupbyisland(islandmap::Vector{Int}, nislands::Int) components = [Int[] for _ in 1:nislands] for (busidx, islandidx) in enumerate(islandmap) push!(components[islandidx], bus_idx) end return components end

function findslackperisland(buses, islandmap, nislands) slackbuses = zeros(Int, nislands)

for i in 1:length(buses)
    if buses.ide[i] == 3  # Slack bus (PSS/E convention)
        island_idx = island_map[i]
        if slack_buses[island_idx] != 0
            @warn "Island $island_idx has multiple slack buses: " *
                  "$(slack_buses[island_idx]) and $i"
        else
            slack_buses[island_idx] = i
        end
    end
end

# Warn about islands without slack
for i in 1:n_islands
    if slack_buses[i] == 0
        @warn "Island $i has no slack bus - power flow may not converge"
    end
end

return slack_buses

end

export TopologyInfo, analyzetopology, analyzetopology!


### Part 4: Island Splitting and Multi-Island Support

Continue in `src/topology/topology.jl`:

julia """ splitislands(sys::SystemModel; autoanalyze::Bool=true) -> Vector{SystemModel}

Extract disconnected islands as separate SystemModel instances.

Returns a vector of SystemModels, one per island. If system has only one island, returns a single-element vector containing the original system.

Each island SystemModel:

  • Has its own AddressManager (independent address space)
  • Has its own IndexOrder (local external→internal mapping)
  • Has its own DAE (independent y, g arrays)
  • Can be solved independently with solve_powerflow()

Arguments

  • sys::SystemModel: Original system
  • auto_analyze::Bool=true: Run topology analysis if not cached

Returns

  • Vector{SystemModel}: One SystemModel per island

Examples

Example 1: Auto-split and solve

sys = SystemModel(case)
islands = split_islands(sys)

if length(islands) == 1
    # Connected system - solve normally
    sol = solve_powerflow(sys)
else
    # Disconnected islands - solve each
    solutions = [solve_powerflow(island) for island in islands]

    # Access results by external bus number
    voltages = get_vars_dict(islands[1], :Bus, :v)
end

Example 2: Parallel solving

using Distributed

islands = split_islands(sys)
solutions = pmap(solve_powerflow, islands)  # Parallel!

Example 3: Contingency analysis

# Open a critical branch
sys.models.Branch.st[42] = 0

# Check if this creates islands
islands = split_islands(sys)
if length(islands) > 1
    @warn "Contingency creates \$(length(islands)) islands!"
end

""" function splitislands(sys::SystemModel; autoanalyze::Bool=true) # Get or compute topology topo = if isnothing(sys.topology) && autoanalyze analyzetopology(sys) elseif !isnothing(sys.topology) sys.topology else error("No topology information. Call analyzetopology!(sys) first or use autoanalyze=true") end

# Single island? Return original system wrapped in vector
if topo.n_islands == 1
    return [sys]
end

@info "Splitting system into $(topo.n_islands) islands"

# Create separate SystemModel for each island
islands = Vector{SystemModel}(undef, topo.n_islands)

for i in 1:topo.n_islands
    islands[i] = _extract_island(sys, topo, i)
end

return islands

end

""" extractisland(sys::SystemModel, topo::TopologyInfo, island_idx::Int) -> SystemModel

Extract a single island as a new SystemModel (internal function). """ function extractisland(sys::SystemModel, topo::TopologyInfo, islandidx::Int) # Get bus mask for this island busmask = topo.islandmap .== islandidx

# Filter models to this island
island_models = _filter_models_to_island(sys.models, sys.order, bus_mask, topo, island_idx)

# Filter external params
island_ext_params = _filter_ext_params_to_island(sys.ext_params, sys.order, bus_mask, island_idx)

# Create new IndexOrder for this island
# This renumbers buses 1:n_buses_island internally while preserving external bus numbers
island_order = _create_island_order(island_models, sys.order, island_idx)

# Create new AddressManager (independent address space)
island_am = AddressManager()

# Create new SystemModel
# auto_setup=true will call setup!() and create DAE
island_sys = SystemModel(
    island_am, island_models;
    ext_params=island_ext_params,
    order=island_order,
    auto_setup=true,
    create_dae=true,
    array_type=sys.array_type,
    parsed_data=nothing,  # Original data belongs to parent
    topology=nothing      # Island is connected by definition (single component)
)

return island_sys

end

""" filtermodelstoisland(models, order, busmask, topo, islandidx) -> NamedTuple

Filter all models to include only instances belonging to specified island. """ function filtermodelstoisland( models::NamedTuple, order::IndexOrder, busmask::BitVector, topo::TopologyInfo, islandidx::Int ) islandmodelsdict = Dict{Symbol, Any}()

for (model_name, model_vec) in pairs(models)
    # Determine which instances belong to this island
    instance_mask = _get_island_mask_for_model(
        model_name, model_vec, order, topo, island_idx
    )

    # Extract instances
    island_subset = model_vec[instance_mask]

    # Only include if non-empty
    if length(island_subset) > 0
        island_models_dict[model_name] = island_subset
    end
end

return NamedTuple(island_models_dict)

end

""" getislandmaskformodel(modelname, modelvec, order, topo, islandidx) -> BitVector

Determine which instances of a model belong to specified island. """ function getislandmaskformodel( modelname::Symbol, modelvec::StructArray, order::IndexOrder, topo::TopologyInfo, islandidx::Int ) n = length(model_vec) mask = falses(n)

if model_name == :Bus
    # Buses: direct mapping via topology
    for i in 1:n
        mask[i] = (topo.island_map[i] == island_idx)
    end

elseif hasfield(eltype(model_vec), :fbus)
    # Branch/Transformer: belongs to island of fbus
    bus_order = order.indices[:Bus]
    for i in 1:n
        fbus_internal = bus_order[model_vec.fbus[i]]
        mask[i] = (topo.island_map[fbus_internal] == island_idx)
    end

elseif hasfield(eltype(model_vec), :bus)
    # PQ/PV/Shunt/etc.: belongs to island of connected bus
    bus_order = order.indices[:Bus]
    for i in 1:n
        bus_internal = bus_order[model_vec.bus[i]]
        mask[i] = (topo.island_map[bus_internal] == island_idx)
    end

else
    # Topological models (Area, Zone, Owner): heuristic assignment
    # Option 1: Assign all to island 1
    # Option 2: Check if any referenced buses are in this island
    # For now: skip with warning
    @warn "Model $model_name has no clear island membership - skipping in island $island_idx"
end

return mask

end

Additional helper functions: filterextparamstoisland, _createisland_order

(Implementation details for filtering external params and creating local IndexOrder)

export split_islands


### Part 5: Multi-Island Variable Access

Create new file: `src/powercore/island_accessors.jl`

julia """ buildunifiedindex(islands::Vector{SystemModel}) -> Dict

Build external key → (islandidx, localinternal_idx) mapping.

Enables lookups across multiple island SystemModels using external bus numbers.

Returns

Dictionary with structure:

Dict(
    :Bus => Dict(ext_bus_num => (island_idx, local_internal_idx), ...),
    :PQ => Dict((bus_num, id) => (island_idx, local_internal_idx), ...),
    ...
)

Example

islands = split_islands(sys)
index = build_unified_index(islands)

# Lookup bus 4001: which island, which local index?
island_idx, local_idx = index[:Bus][4001]

""" function buildunifiedindex(islands::Vector{SystemModel}) unified_index = Dict{Symbol, Dict}()

for (island_idx, island_sys) in enumerate(islands)
    if isnothing(island_sys.order)
        error("Island $island_idx has no IndexOrder - cannot build unified index")
    end

    # For each model type in this island
    for (model_name, key_to_internal) in pairs(island_sys.order.indices)
        # Initialize model dict if first time seeing this model
        if !haskey(unified_index, model_name)
            unified_index[model_name] = Dict()
        end

        # Add all instances from this island
        for (ext_key, local_internal_idx) in key_to_internal
            unified_index[model_name][ext_key] = (island_idx, local_internal_idx)
        end
    end
end

return unified_index

end

""" getvarmulti(islands::Vector{SystemModel}, model::Symbol, var::Symbol, ext_key)

Get variable value across multiple islands using external key.

Automatically determines which island contains the requested instance and retrieves the value.

Example

islands = split_islands(sys)

# Get voltage for bus 4001 (automatically finds correct island)
v = get_var_multi(islands, :Bus, :v, 4001)

Performance Note

This function builds the unified index on each call. For multiple queries, consider building the index once:

index = build_unified_index(islands)
# Then use get_var_multi_cached(islands, index, ...)

""" function getvarmulti(islands::Vector{SystemModel}, model::Symbol, var::Symbol, extkey) # Build index (could be optimized by caching) index = buildunified_index(islands)

# Lookup which island contains this instance
if !haskey(index, model)
    error("Model :$model not found in any island")
end
if !haskey(index[model], ext_key)
    error("External key $ext_key not found for model :$model in any island")
end

island_idx, local_internal_idx = index[model][ext_key]

# Get from the appropriate island
island = islands[island_idx]
return get_var_by_index(island, model, var, local_internal_idx)

end

""" getvarmulticached(islands, index, model, var, extkey)

Get variable value using pre-computed unified index (faster). """ function getvarmulticached( islands::Vector{SystemModel}, index::Dict{Symbol, Dict}, model::Symbol, var::Symbol, extkey ) islandidx, localinternalidx = index[model][extkey] island = islands[islandidx] return getvarbyindex(island, model, var, localinternalidx) end

""" getallvars_multi(islands::Vector{SystemModel}, model::Symbol, var::Symbol) -> Dict

Get all variable values across all islands, keyed by external keys.

Example

islands = split_islands(sys)

# Get all bus voltages from all islands
voltages = get_all_vars_multi(islands, :Bus, :v)
# Dict(1 => 1.06, 2 => 1.045, 4001 => 1.02, ...) across all islands

""" function getallvars_multi(islands::Vector{SystemModel}, model::Symbol, var::Symbol) result = Dict()

for island in islands
    island_values = get_vars_dict(island, model, var)
    merge!(result, island_values)
end

return result

end

export buildunifiedindex export getvarmulti, getvarmulticached, getallvarsmulti

### Terminal-ExtParam Unification ✅ COMPLETED (Breaking Change)

**Context:** During Phase 4 implementation, we discovered that Terminal (topology) and ExtParam (data retrieval) both encoded connectivity information separately, violating DRY principles.

**Solution:** Refactored ExtParam to use Terminal as base type, creating a single source of truth for model connectivity.

**Changes Made:**
1. Moved `Terminal` struct to `core_types.jl`
2. Refactored `ExtParam` to contain `terminal::Terminal` field
3. Updated all models to declare `TERMINALS` constants
4. Updated `ext2int.jl`, `system.jl`, `per_unit.jl` to use Terminal API
5. Fixed all tests (420 tests passing)

**Breaking Change:**

julia

OLD

ExtParam(:basekv, :terminal, :Bus, :basekv, :i, BaseVoltage(), ...)

NEW

ExtParam(:basekv, Terminal(:Bus, :i), :basekv, BaseVoltage(), ...)


**Rationale:** This breaking change was necessary to eliminate technical debt and ensure Terminal API is the authoritative source for all connectivity information.

**Implementation:** See [core_types.jl](../../src/foundation/core_types.jl), all model files, and related infrastructure.

**Estimated effort:** 6-8 hours (completed)

## Migration Strategy

### For Existing Code

**Existing solver code continues to work:**

julia

Old pattern (still valid)

dae = DAE(Float64, sys) ws = SystemResidualWorkspace(Float64, sys) evaluatesystemresiduals!(ws, dae)

New pattern (optional)

sys.dae created automatically

ws = SystemResidualWorkspace(Float64, sys) evaluatesystemresiduals!(ws, sys.dae)


**Variable access migration:**

julia

Old pattern (manual)

am = sys.addressmanager vaddrs = getvaraddresses(am, :Bus, :v) busidx = sys.order.indices[:Bus][busnum] voltage = dae.y[vaddrs[busidx]]

New pattern (generic)

voltage = getvar(sys, :Bus, :v, busnum)


### Deprecation Timeline

**Version 1.x (current):**
- Add new features (DAE field, accessors, topology)
- Keep all existing patterns working
- Mark nothing as deprecated

**Version 2.0 (future):**
- Recommend new patterns in docs
- Keep old patterns working with deprecation warnings
- Add migration guide

**Version 3.0 (far future):**
- Remove deprecated patterns
- Require use of new accessors for variable access

## Benefits Summary

### Code Reduction
- **Before:** 100+ model-specific getter/setter functions
- **After:** ~10 generic functions handle everything

### Consistency
- **Before:** Different access patterns per model type
- **After:** One pattern for all: `get_var(sys, model, var, key)`

### Islands Support
- **Before:** Would require new container types and specialized methods
- **After:** Islands are just `Vector{SystemModel}`, same interface

### User Experience
- **Before:** "How do I get bus 4001's voltage?" → Read docs, find function
- **After:** `get_var(sys, :Bus, :v, 4001)` - consistent, discoverable

### Extensibility
- **Before:** New model → write new accessor functions
- **After:** New model → accessors work automatically via AddressManager

## Future Enhancements

### 1. Cached Unified Index

julia

Compute once, reuse many times

struct IslandCollection islands::Vector{SystemModel} unified_index::Dict{Symbol, Dict} end

function IslandCollection(islands::Vector{SystemModel}) index = buildunifiedindex(islands) IslandCollection(islands, index) end

Fast lookups

getvar(ic::IslandCollection, model, var, key) = getvarmulticached(ic.islands, ic.unified_index, model, var, key)


### 2. Broadcasting Support

julia

Get multiple variables at once

busnums = [1, 2, 3, 4] voltages = getvar.(Ref(sys), :Bus, :v, bus_nums)


### 3. NamedTuple Interface

julia

More ergonomic for scripting

bus = get_bus(sys, 4001)

NamedTuple(v=1.02, theta=0.05, p=0.5, q=0.2)


### 4. DataFrame Export

julia using DataFrames

Export results to DataFrame

df = to_dataframe(sys, :Bus, [:v, :theta])

DataFrame with columns: bus_num, v, theta


### 5. Visualization Hooks

julia

One-liner plotting

plotvoltages(sys) # Uses getvarsdict internally plotisland_topology(islands) ```

Conclusion

This design provides:

  1. Clean architecture: DAE as integral part of SystemModel
  2. Generic interface: One set of functions for all variable access
  3. Natural islands: No special containers, just Vector{SystemModel}
  4. Minimal changes: ~30-40 hours implementation, no breaking changes
  5. Future-proof: Easy to extend for new models and use cases

Key insight: AddressManager + IndexOrder + DAE gives us complete generic access to any variable in any model with zero model-specific code. Islands extend naturally by using the same SystemModel type at different scales.
